title: API protocols: REST, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, SSE
status: TEMPLATE SLICE. This domain is the reference format for the other 36.
why_this_domain_first: It exercises every layer of the design: capture, schema recovery, hypothesis, test, oracle, defense. If the format works here it works everywhere.

atom_notes.A01: schema and query strings reach an interpreter, the GraphQL and SQL injection family
atom_notes.A02: object level and function level authorization, the BOLA and BFLA family
atom_notes.A03: token or identity confusion across API versions, gateways and microservices
atom_notes.A05: type and shape confusion, mass assignment, duplicate keys, null coercion
atom_notes.A06: path and route confusion, versioning, shadow routes, gateway vs service routing
atom_notes.A10: business logic in stateful endpoints, sequence and quota abuse
atom_notes.A12: race conditions in idempotent looking endpoints
atom_notes.A16: the API is an LLM or agent endpoint, tool calls and prompt injection

required_cells.why: you cannot test an API you have not enumerated
route and parameter discovery at scale is the highest yield API step
schema to hypothesis: what is likely broken given this shape
automated probing with a real oracle, not a scanner's guess
BOLA and BFLA exploitation needs two identities and object ids
proof with a negative control, the difference between a finding and a guess
API findings need impact framing or they get closed as informational
retest after fix, nobody covers this
continuous schema diff, new endpoints appear weekly

entries.name: kiterunner
entries.role: API route brute force with real-world route wordlists
preconditions: API routes are guessable from naming conventions
no global 404 normalisation
entries.note: The route wordlists matter more than the tool. Assetnote's kite files encode real API shapes.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: capture one authenticated request from the API
kr scan <host> -w routes.kite -x 8, wait for 429 before raising
diff the discovered routes against the captured set, the delta is the target

entries.name: ffuf
entries.role: Generic fuzzer, the fallback when a protocol specific tool does not exist
preconditions: a fuzz position exists in the request
entries.note: Set -rate. An agent that ignores rate is a denial of service, not a tester.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: pick one fuzz position and one signal, status or size
ffuf -w list -u URL -of json -rate 30
re-run the top hits with a control value that should 404

entries.name: arjun
entries.role: HTTP parameter discovery, including parameters the API does not document
preconditions: the server accepts parameters it does not advertise
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: arjun -u endpoint -oJ params.json
for each new parameter, send it with a benign value and with an absurd one
the parameter that changes behaviour is the hypothesis

entries.name: clairvoyance
entries.role: Recover a GraphQL schema when introspection is disabled
preconditions: introspection disabled but field suggestions enabled
or error messages leak field names
detected_by: introspection query signature and field suggestion probing
entries.note: This is the canonical example of a tool that exists because a defence (introspection off) was assumed sufficient and was not.
procedure: confirm introspection is actually off with a direct query
clairvoyance -o schema.json -w wordlist URL/graphql
compare recovered fields to what the UI calls, the gap is unauthorised surface

entries.name: InQL
entries.role: Introspection to ready-made queries, one per field, plus IDE integration
preconditions: introspection enabled, or schema otherwise obtained
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: inql -t URL/graphql -o out
pick the mutation with the most privileged sounding name
send it with a minimal body and read the error, the error describes the input shape

entries.name: graphw00f
entries.role: GraphQL engine fingerprint, decides which defence bypass class applies
preconditions: an exposed graphql endpoint
entries.note: Engine matters because batching, alias limits and introspection quirks differ per engine. Fingerprint before you payload.
procedure: graphw00f -d -t URL/graphql
note engine and version
look up that engine's introspection and batching quirks before payload selection

entries.name: mitmproxy2swagger
entries.role: Turn captured traffic into an OpenAPI spec, the reverse of codegen
preconditions: you captured real traffic from a real client
entries.note: The single highest leverage API step. A spec turns guessing into property testing.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: mitmdump -w flows while using the product normally
mitmproxy2swagger -i flows -o spec.yml -p https://api
open spec.yml, every path marked ignored is a question: why did it not match

entries.name: grpcurl
entries.role: gRPC reflection, describe and call, the whole gRPC surface
preconditions: server reflection enabled, common in internal services exposed by mistake
entries.note: Reflection on is equivalent to a free full schema. Nobody checks it.
procedure: grpcurl -plaintext host:443 list
if reflection answers, describe every service
call the least privileged looking method with an empty message and read the field error

entries.name: schemathesis
entries.role: Property based testing from an OpenAPI or GraphQL schema
preconditions: a schema exists, real or recovered
detected_by: introspection query signature and field suggestion probing
entries.note: Reproducible failures with hypothesis seeds, which makes it usable as evidence.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: obtain or recover a spec
schemathesis run spec.yml --checks all --hypothesis-seed 0
for each failure, replay with the recorded seed, that is the evidence

entries.name: RESTler
entries.role: Stateful REST fuzzing, finds sequences that single call scanners cannot see
preconditions: multi step API with producer and consumer endpoints
OpenAPI spec available
entries.note: The only credible stateful API fuzzer. Heavy build, worth it for logic bugs.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: restler compile --api_spec spec.json, this generates the grammar
restler test --grammar_file g.json, then restler fuzz
inspect sequence bugs, they need more than one call to reproduce

entries.name: graphql-cop
entries.role: GraphQL misconfiguration audit, the cheap wins first
preconditions: graphql endpoint reachable
detected_by: introspection query signature and field suggestion probing
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: graphql-cop -t URL/graphql
take each finding and confirm it by hand, the tool over-reports
record the response, not the tool verdict

entries.name: Damn Vulnerable GraphQL Application
entries.role: Practice target that exercises the whole GraphQL attack set
preconditions: you want a lab, not a target
entries.note: Use this to calibrate a tool before pointing it at a real target. A tool that fails DVGA is a broken tool.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: docker run the DVGA image
run the tool under evaluation against it
if the tool cannot solve the known bugs, do not point it at a real target

entries.name: OWASP crAPI
entries.role: Completely Ridiculous API, a full microservice target with all Top 10 classes
preconditions: lab
entries.note: Best API lab for BOLA because it has real object ownership and multiple users.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: docker compose up crAPI
create two users and one object owned by user A
replay A's object requests as B, that is the BOLA harness

entries.name: VAmPI
entries.role: Small vulnerable API, fastest way to smoke test an agent
preconditions: lab
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: docker run VAmPI
enumerate with the tool
use only as a smoke test, it is too small to be a benchmark

entries.name: jwt_tool
entries.role: JWT attack set, alg confusion, none, kid traversal, jku injection
preconditions: token based auth with a JWT you can decode
entries.note: In D06 mostly, listed here because every API test hits tokens first.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: jwt_tool <token> -M at, run the full set
for each success, verify the token actually grants something
the accepted token with no privilege difference is not a finding

entries.name: Cherrybomb
entries.role: OpenAPI spec audit, undocumented auth, missing rate limit, weak schema
preconditions: openapi spec
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: cherrybomb -f spec.yml
each finding is a spec defect, confirm against the live API
the ones that survive contact with the API are the report

entries.name: Akto
entries.role: API discovery and testing platform, runs tests against traffic
preconditions: mirrored traffic or a reachable API
entries.note: Useful when you want automated coverage over many endpoints, weak on logic.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: point akto at mirrored traffic or a reachable API
run its test suite for the detected API shapes
triage by whether the endpoint holds objects, not by severity

entries.name: Astra
entries.role: REST API security scanner, auth and injection across swagger
preconditions: swagger or postman collection
entries.note: Last release is old. Kept because nothing newer covers swagger native auth testing the same way.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: astra --url spec.json
review auth findings first, they are the highest hit rate
ignore the injection findings until you have confirmed one by hand

entries.name: BatchQL
entries.role: GraphQL batching and query name based attacks, rate limit bypass
preconditions: batching enabled, or query name allows cost bypass
entries.note: Targets a defence (rate limiting) that assumes one request equals one operation.
procedure: confirm batching is enabled with a two alias query
send N aliases of one mutation against one rate limited endpoint
compare operation count to request count, that ratio is the finding

entries.name: GraphQLmap
entries.role: GraphQL exploitation console, dump schema, inject, escalate
preconditions: graphql endpoint
detected_by: introspection query signature and field suggestion probing
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: graphqlmap -u URL/graphql
dump schema if introspection is on, otherwise skip to injection modules
confirm any dump against a second query, never trust one tool

entries.name: newman
entries.role: Run a postman collection, the cheapest way to replay an authenticated flow
preconditions: a collection exists, or you built one from a HAR
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: export the collection from captured traffic
run it as identity A, save the responses
run it as identity B, diff, the diffs are the access matrix

entries.name: OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023)
entries.role: The taxonomy every API finding should map to
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: map each finding to exactly one of A1 to A10
if it maps to none, the finding is probably not an API issue
use the mapping in the report, it is what the client recognises

entries.name: MindAPI
entries.role: Decision tree for API testing, the manual equivalent of this domain
entries.note: Closest prior art to what this repo does. It is a mind map, not machine readable, which is the gap we fill.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: walk the mind map for the protocol in front of you
each leaf is a test you have not run
record negatives, the map's value is coverage not hits

entries.name: API-Security-Checklist
entries.role: Defensive checklist, useful as the mirror for every offensive row
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
procedure: read the section matching the finding class
each countermeasure is the control column for your report
any countermeasure missing at the target is a hardening recommendation

entries.name: APIFuzzer
entries.role: Fuzzes a running API from its OpenAPI spec, no source needed
preconditions: an OpenAPI spec and a reachable API
oracle: crash or status violation against the spec

entries.name: CATS
entries.role: OpenAPI fuzzer that generates tests from the schema and reports by category
preconditions: an OpenAPI spec
oracle: fuzz report per rule with a reproducible request

entries.name: EvoMaster
entries.role: Evolutionary API test generator, reaches states a rule based fuzzer does not
preconditions: an API with stateful endpoints
oracle: a sequence that violates an invariant
entries.note: Slow and needs setup. Justified when dependencies between calls matter, which is most real APIs.

entries.name: graphql-wordlist
entries.role: Field and type name corpus for schema recovery when introspection is off
preconditions: introspection disabled but suggestions or errors leak
entries.note: Pairs with clairvoyance. The wordlist quality decides the recovery rate.

entries.name: Optic
entries.role: API spec diffing and linting, the fastest way to spot a breaking change between versions
preconditions: two specs, or live traffic and a spec

entries.name: REST API Goat
entries.role: Deliberately vulnerable API for practising the whole Top 10
preconditions: docker

entries.name: Swagger-EZ
entries.role: Turns a swagger file into a testing surface with auth handling
preconditions: a swagger document

entries.name: TnT-Fuzzer
entries.role: OpenAPI 3 fuzzer focused on parameter and body mutation
preconditions: an OpenAPI 3 spec

entries.name: Step CI
entries.role: Declarative API test runner, useful for replaying an authorised workflow as evidence
preconditions: a workflow description
oracle: assertion pass or fail per step
entries.note: Reproducible evidence matters more than coverage here. A commit-able test is a better finding than a screenshot.

entries.name: API-SecurityEmpire
entries.role: Curated API security resource set, useful as a completeness cross check

entries.name: APISandbox
entries.role: Deliberately weak API sandbox covering the OWASP API flaws
preconditions: docker

entries.name: ShipFast API protection walkthrough
entries.role: A worked API protection lab with client and server, good for testing whether a tool handles a real app
preconditions: docker

entries.name: 31 Days of API Security Tips
entries.role: Practical tips corpus, the kind of thing that fills gaps a taxonomy misses

tree.q: Do you have a schema or a capture for this API?
tree.why: Everything downstream depends on this. Guessing without a schema is the least efficient mode and the most common mistake.

branches.a: Yes, OpenAPI or GraphQL schema in hand

next.q: Is the schema generated by the vendor or recovered by you?
Does the live API match the spec on undocumented fields?
next.action: diff spec against live responses, undocumented fields are the finding surface

next.q: Are there endpoints in the client that traffic never touched?
next.action: bundle and mobile artifact diff against the captured endpoint set

branches.a: No schema, only a live endpoint

branches.action: fingerprint engine, try introspection, if off recover fields by suggestion abuse
attempt reflection, then describe, then call with empty message to map fields
capture one authenticated session, convert to spec, then fuzz from the spec
record frames, look for client side trust and message type confusion

mirror.detect: object id enumeration pattern per session
mirror.control: object level authorisation check on every read, not on the list endpoint
function level authorisation, deny by default

mirror.detect: introspection query signature and field suggestion probing
mirror.control: disable suggestions too, not just introspection
mirror.rule: query depth and suggestion error rate

mirror.control: cost analysis per operation, not per request
explicit allowlist binding, never object hydration from body

mirror.detect: live response shape differs from spec
same token accepted by services with different audiences

gaps.gap: No tool recovers a GraphQL schema when both introspection and suggestions are off
gaps.build_candidate: differential error oracle that recovers field names from validation messages, then type names from union errors

gaps.gap: No tool diffs a client bundle's endpoint set against captured traffic automatically
gaps.build_candidate: join rea analyze_web_bundle routes with rea inspect_web_network_capture urls, emit the set difference

gaps.gap: No tool tests object level authorisation across N users automatically
gaps.build_candidate: create M identities, replay every captured object request as each identity, flag any 200 that should be 403
frame schema inference from capture plus type confusion mutations

gaps.gap: No tool verifies a fix without a full rescan
gaps.build_candidate: store the exact request that proved the finding, replay it as the retest, diff the oracle

gaps.gap: L10 impact framing and L11 retest cells are empty in this domain
gaps.build_candidate: impact template per API class plus a retest harness

unreviewed_index.note: Entries from the corpus that mention API but were not enriched for this slice are listed in data/domains/D11.index.json, not here. The gap between indexed and enriched is reported, never hidden.
